title: No commandment, prayer, or virtue without effort; sin and desire ensnare
english: Just as a scale cannot balance when one side is weighed down, so no one can accomplish God's commandment while the fleshly mind prevails over him. Just as no one can learn a craft without devoting himself to it diligently, so no one can acquire prayer without persevering before God in uprightness of heart. The one who has not acquired pure prayer has no weapon for battle. The one adorned and swept clean, yet devoid of God's virtues, will be a dwelling for demons. Just as a king cannot dwell in a poor man's house, so Christ will not dwell in a soul defiled from sin. Just as wild land is tamed through diligent cultivation, so a soul made wild by sins is tamed if it will conduct itself by God's law. Just as a rock in the sea remains firm and unshaken when battered by waves, so the one who has accomplished the virtues and been wholly mixed with them will never be shaken by the devil. Just as a physician devises a remedy for the healing of a disease, so the knowledge of God, when preserved, teaches the one who partakes of it how to be kept safe and advance to greater things. Just as a ravine makes its own passage, so sin, once admitted, brings about the destruction of the one who possesses it. Just as a deer that has fallen into nets cannot easily escape, so the one who carries out his desires and lives in this world will not escape sin; for evil desires and pleasures are bonds hard to loosen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his chain of comparisons, now showing that keeping God's commandment, acquiring prayer, and standing firm in virtue all require effort, while sin and desire trap the one who accepts them.

title: The vine, the arrow, the Trinity, and the fire
english: Just as a vine that does not produce good fruit is cut out so that it does not make the place useless, so everyone who does not produce the fruits of the Holy Spirit will be rooted out by the Lord. Just as it is impossible for a person struck by an arrow not to be harmed, so it is impossible for a monk who has accepted an evil thought not to be wounded. Just as one who leaves the straight road wanders in a foreign land, not knowing where he is going, so a person who does not believe in the Trinity one in being wanders. Just as something divided into many parts is one in nature, so the Holy Trinity, though divided in names and persons, is one in nature. You could not grasp the nature of God, not even if you flew with wings; God is incomprehensible, and for this reason he is also our Creator. Just as a vessel being made does not know the origin and nature of its maker, so a person will not be able to discover the nature or origin of God. Do not busy yourself about the Trinity, but only believe and worship; for the one who busies himself about it does not believe.

Acquire wisdom and not silver; make for yourselves a shining garment of Christ our Lord, beyond every linen robe, because possessions will not help in the day of death. Just as fire consumes a thicket, so every sinner will be consumed by the eternal fire, and he cannot die; for he will be tormented immortally.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his chain of comparisons, now turning to the fate of the fruitless, the wound of an evil thought, the error of not believing in the Trinity one in being, and the eternal fire awaiting sinners.

title: No Excuse for Disobedience
english: It is nothing great if we become righteous, for what God first created us to be—very good—that is what we will become. The one who lives against nature does not keep God's commandments. All wisdom is to fear the Lord, and all teaching that does not teach the law of the Lord is foolishness and folly. Faith and baptism will not rescue from the eternal fire without works of righteousness.

For if you enlist with Christ, keep his commandments; and if you believe in the things to come, lay hold of eternal glory and fear the flaming sword. If you do not accomplish God's commands, do not call yourself faithful. All creation obeys the command of God, but man alone disobeys—the one for whom all things were made. We will offer God nothing by keeping ourselves pure; rather, we will procure life for ourselves and the inexpressible enjoyment of eternal good things.

Do not say, 'I cannot keep God's commandment because of father or mother or wife or children or anyone else,' for they will not rescue you from the impending wrath and the endless worm. Let everyone who opposes you in the accomplishment of God's will and the virtues be abominable and hateful to you; it is not even good to eat with such a person.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius is closing his exhortation to monks, insisting that faith and baptism do not save without works and that no human tie excuses breaking God's commandment.
